evidence: Ngu Xa Island, or Đảo ngọc Ngũ Xã in Vietnamese, is a small, crescent-shaped strip of land nestled peacefully beside Trúc Bạch Lake in Ba Dinh District, Hanoi. This unique island, resembling a floating lotus flower, has been a hub of cultural and culinary significance since the 17th century, when artisans from five bronze casting villages gathered here to establish their livelihoods, giving birth to the name Ngũ Xã, honoring the essence of the ancient Thăng Long bronze casting craft.
